en.text:
Today’s M&A briefing — 6 deals, the strategies behind them · 23 November 2026

🔹 FedEx (à la tête d'un consortium) (american express delivery and logistics group, with a global presence) finalizes the acquisition of InPost (operator of automated parcel lockers and out-of-home delivery for e-commerce, primarily in Central and Western Europe) — €7.8bn.
InPost operates tens of thousands of collection points enabling time-flexible delivery at a lower cost than home delivery.
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: InPost's lockers are capillary physical assets impossible to replicate quickly, comparable to a telecom tower network: their value grows with each new online merchant that connects to them.

🔹 CTP (european developer and operator of logistics and industrial parks, listed in Amsterdam, active primarily) acquires SLP (Strategic Logistics Park) (developer of logistics parks in Vietnam).
Vietnam has become a preferred destination for industrial relocation from China (electronics, textiles, automotive components), driven by Sino-American trade tensions.
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: CTP exports its model of long-term ownership and operation of industrial parks to Vietnam, betting on the permanence of global production chain diversification rather than a short cycle.

🔹 EDF (energy supplier to individuals and businesses in the UK, under the EDF Energy brand) intends to acquire Utilita (british energy supplier specializing in prepayment meters, primarily for low-income households).
The acquisition would allow EDF to exceed six million energy accounts in the UK. The prepayment meter is a structurally distinct segment of the standard residential market, with a specific clientele, billing infrastructure, and regulation.
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: Beyond volume, EDF gains access to a customer base whose granular relationship with energy gains value in a market where demand flexibility becomes an asset in itself.

🔹 Swietelsky (austrian construction and railway engineering group, present in many European countries) acquires VIKING-Rail (danish rail freight operator).
Rail freight in Northern Europe is undergoing progressive consolidation, driven by regulatory pressure for modal shift and network liberalization.

🔹 État portugais repurchases REN (Redes Energéticas Nacionais) (operator of the electricity and natural gas transmission network in Portugal).

🔹 Schroeder van der Kolk (the Hague-based company) takes over Big Bazar (dutch discount retail chain).
The discount segment remains under pressure in the Netherlands, caught between food hard-discounters and online retail.

fr.text:
M&A : les 6 annonces récentes de l'édito du 23 novembre 2026.

🔹 FedEx (à la tête d'un consortium) (𝑔𝑟𝑜𝑢𝑝𝑒 𝑎𝑚𝑒́𝑟𝑖𝑐𝑎𝑖𝑛 𝑑𝑒 𝑙𝑖𝑣𝑟𝑎𝑖𝑠𝑜𝑛 𝑒𝑥𝑝𝑟𝑒𝑠𝑠 𝑒𝑡 𝑙𝑜𝑔𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒, 𝑝𝑟𝑒́𝑠𝑒𝑛𝑡 𝑑𝑎𝑛𝑠 𝑙𝑒 𝑚𝑜𝑛𝑑𝑒 𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑖𝑒𝑟) finalise le rachat de InPost (𝑜𝑝𝑒́𝑟𝑎𝑡𝑒𝑢𝑟 𝑑𝑒 𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑠𝑖𝑔𝑛𝑒𝑠 𝑎𝑢𝑡𝑜𝑚𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒𝑠 𝑒𝑡 𝑑𝑒 𝑙𝑖𝑣𝑟𝑎𝑖𝑠𝑜𝑛 ℎ𝑜𝑟𝑠 𝑑𝑜𝑚𝑖𝑐𝑖𝑙𝑒 𝑝𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑙𝑒 𝑒-𝑐𝑜𝑚𝑚𝑒𝑟𝑐𝑒, 𝑝𝑟𝑖𝑛𝑐𝑖𝑝𝑎𝑙𝑒𝑚𝑒𝑛𝑡 𝑒𝑛 𝐸𝑢𝑟𝑜𝑝𝑒 𝑐𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑟𝑎𝑙𝑒 𝑒𝑡 𝑜𝑐𝑐𝑖𝑑𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑎𝑙𝑒) — 7,8 Md€.
InPost exploite des dizaines de milliers de points de collecte permettant une livraison sans contrainte horaire à un coût inférieur à la livraison à domicile.
𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝗱𝗲 𝘃𝘂𝗲 : Les lockers d'InPost sont des actifs physiques capillaires impossibles à répliquer rapidement, comparables à un réseau de tours télécoms : leur valeur croît avec chaque nouveau commerçant en ligne qui s'y connecte.

🔹 CTP (𝑑𝑒́𝑣𝑒𝑙𝑜𝑝𝑝𝑒𝑢𝑟 𝑒𝑡 𝑜𝑝𝑒́𝑟𝑎𝑡𝑒𝑢𝑟 𝑒𝑢𝑟𝑜𝑝𝑒́𝑒𝑛 𝑑𝑒 𝑝𝑎𝑟𝑐𝑠 𝑙𝑜𝑔𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒𝑠 𝑒𝑡 𝑖𝑛𝑑𝑢𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑖𝑒𝑙𝑠, 𝑐𝑜𝑡𝑒́ 𝑎̀ 𝐴𝑚𝑠𝑡𝑒𝑟𝑑𝑎𝑚, 𝑎𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑓 𝑝𝑟𝑖𝑛𝑐𝑖𝑝𝑎𝑙𝑒𝑚𝑒𝑛𝑡 𝑒𝑛 𝐸𝑢𝑟𝑜𝑝𝑒 𝑐𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑟𝑎𝑙𝑒 𝑒𝑡 𝑜𝑟𝑖𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑎𝑙𝑒) acquiert SLP (Strategic Logistics Park) (𝑑𝑒́𝑣𝑒𝑙𝑜𝑝𝑝𝑒𝑢𝑟 𝑑𝑒 𝑝𝑎𝑟𝑐𝑠 𝑙𝑜𝑔𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒𝑠 𝑎𝑢 𝑉𝑖𝑒𝑡𝑛𝑎𝑚).
Le Vietnam est devenu une destination privilégiée de la relocalisation industrielle depuis la Chine (électronique, textile, composants automobiles), portée par les tensions commerciales sino-américaines.

🔹 EDF (𝑓𝑜𝑢𝑟𝑛𝑖𝑠𝑠𝑒𝑢𝑟 𝑑'𝑒́𝑛𝑒𝑟𝑔𝑖𝑒 𝑎𝑢𝑥 𝑝𝑎𝑟𝑡𝑖𝑐𝑢𝑙𝑖𝑒𝑟𝑠 𝑒𝑡 𝑎𝑢𝑥 𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑟𝑒𝑝𝑟𝑖𝑠𝑒𝑠 𝑎𝑢 𝑅𝑜𝑦𝑎𝑢𝑚𝑒-𝑈𝑛𝑖, 𝑠𝑜𝑢𝑠 𝑙𝑎 𝑚𝑎𝑟𝑞𝑢𝑒 𝐸𝐷𝐹 𝐸𝑛𝑒𝑟𝑔𝑦) souhaite acquérir Utilita (𝑓𝑜𝑢𝑟𝑛𝑖𝑠𝑠𝑒𝑢𝑟 𝑏𝑟𝑖𝑡𝑎𝑛𝑛𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒 𝑑'𝑒́𝑛𝑒𝑟𝑔𝑖𝑒 𝑠𝑝𝑒́𝑐𝑖𝑎𝑙𝑖𝑠𝑒́).
L'acquisition permettrait à EDF de franchir le seuil de six millions de comptes énergie au Royaume-Uni.

🔹 Swietelsky (𝑔𝑟𝑜𝑢𝑝𝑒 𝑎𝑢𝑡𝑟𝑖𝑐ℎ𝑖𝑒𝑛 𝑑𝑒 𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑢𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑒𝑡 𝑑'𝑖𝑛𝑔𝑒́𝑛𝑖𝑒𝑟𝑖𝑒 𝑓𝑒𝑟𝑟𝑜𝑣𝑖𝑎𝑖𝑟𝑒, 𝑝𝑟𝑒́𝑠𝑒𝑛𝑡 𝑑𝑎𝑛𝑠 𝑑𝑒 𝑛𝑜𝑚𝑏𝑟𝑒𝑢𝑥 𝑝𝑎𝑦𝑠 𝑒𝑢𝑟𝑜𝑝𝑒́𝑒𝑛𝑠) acquiert VIKING-Rail (𝑜𝑝𝑒́𝑟𝑎𝑡𝑒𝑢𝑟 𝑑𝑎𝑛𝑜𝑖𝑠 𝑑𝑒 𝑓𝑟𝑒𝑡 𝑓𝑒𝑟𝑟𝑜𝑣𝑖𝑎𝑖𝑟𝑒).

🔹 État portugais rachète REN (Redes Energéticas Nacionais) (𝑜𝑝𝑒́𝑟𝑎𝑡𝑒𝑢𝑟 𝑑𝑢 𝑟𝑒́𝑠𝑒𝑎𝑢 𝑑𝑒 𝑡𝑟𝑎𝑛𝑠𝑝𝑜𝑟𝑡 𝑑'𝑒́𝑙𝑒𝑐𝑡𝑟𝑖𝑐𝑖𝑡𝑒́ 𝑒𝑡 𝑑𝑒 𝑔𝑎𝑧 𝑛𝑎𝑡𝑢𝑟𝑒𝑙 𝑎𝑢 𝑃𝑜𝑟𝑡𝑢𝑔𝑎𝑙).

🔹 Schroeder van der Kolk (𝑠𝑜𝑐𝑖𝑒́𝑡𝑒́ 𝑏𝑎𝑠𝑒́𝑒 𝑎̀ 𝐿𝑎 𝐻𝑎𝑦𝑒) reprend Big Bazar (𝑐ℎ𝑎𝑖̂𝑛𝑒 𝑑𝑒 𝑑𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑖𝑏𝑢𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑑𝑖𝑠𝑐𝑜𝑢𝑛𝑡 𝑛𝑒́𝑒𝑟𝑙𝑎𝑛𝑑𝑎𝑖𝑠𝑒).
Le segment discount reste sous pression aux Pays-Bas, pris entre les hard-discounters alimentaires et le commerce en ligne.

en.text:
Today’s fundraising briefing — 2 deals, the strategies behind them · 23 November 2026

🔹 AlpSemi (development of power semiconductors for smart grids, based in Grenoble) — €17m.
AlpSemi is located in the Grenoble ecosystem, where public microelectronics research (CEA-Leti, STMicroelectronics) and industrial start-ups coexist with sufficient density to design components of this level of complexity.
𝗜𝗻𝘃𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀: Yotta Capital, French fund.
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: Power semiconductors are one of the least visible but most structural bottlenecks of the energy transition, in a segment where European dependence on Asian suppliers is real.

🔹 Vetaion (development of robots to automate the manufacturing of electrical control cabinets for industrial installations, based in Munich) — €5.7m · pre-seed.
The production of control cabinets remains largely manual and fragmented among hundreds of small integrators, with each industrial project requiring a specific version — a barrier that Vetaion seeks to overcome with robotics.
𝗜𝗻𝘃𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀: Visionaries Tomorrow and UVC Partners (co-leads).
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: If Vetaion succeeds in automating this process, it is not just selling robots: it is redefining the business model of an entire segment of industrial subcontracting that employs tens of thousands of technicians in Europe.

Levées de fonds : les 2 opérations chiffrées de l'édito du 23 novembre 2026.

🔹 AlpSemi (𝑑𝑒́𝑣𝑒𝑙𝑜𝑝𝑝𝑒𝑚𝑒𝑛𝑡 𝑑𝑒 𝑠𝑒𝑚𝑖-𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑑𝑢𝑐𝑡𝑒𝑢𝑟𝑠 𝑑𝑒 𝑝𝑢𝑖𝑠𝑠𝑎𝑛𝑐𝑒 𝑝𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑙𝑒𝑠 𝑟𝑒́𝑠𝑒𝑎𝑢𝑥 𝑒́𝑙𝑒𝑐𝑡𝑟𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒𝑠 𝑖𝑛𝑡𝑒𝑙𝑙𝑖𝑔𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑠, 𝑏𝑎𝑠𝑒́𝑒 𝑎̀ 𝐺𝑟𝑒𝑛𝑜𝑏𝑙𝑒) — 17 M€.
AlpSemi est implantée dans l'écosystème grenoblois, où la recherche publique en micro-électronique (CEA-Leti, STMicroelectronics) et les start-up industrielles coexistent avec une densité suffisante pour concevoir des composants de ce niveau de complexité.
𝗔𝘃𝗲𝗰 : Yotta Capital, fonds français.
𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝗱𝗲 𝘃𝘂𝗲 : Les semi-conducteurs de puissance sont l'un des goulets d'étranglement les moins visibles mais les plus structurants de la transition énergétique, dans un segment où la dépendance européenne vis-à-vis des fournisseurs asiatiques est réelle.

🔹 Vetaion (𝑑𝑒́𝑣𝑒𝑙𝑜𝑝𝑝𝑒𝑚𝑒𝑛𝑡 𝑑𝑒 𝑟𝑜𝑏𝑜𝑡𝑠 𝑝𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑎𝑢𝑡𝑜𝑚𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑠𝑒𝑟 𝑙𝑎 𝑓𝑎𝑏𝑟𝑖𝑐𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑑'𝑎𝑟𝑚𝑜𝑖𝑟𝑒𝑠 𝑑𝑒 𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑡𝑟𝑜̂𝑙𝑒 𝑒́𝑙𝑒𝑐𝑡𝑟𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒) — 5,7 M€ · pré-seed.
La production d'armoires de contrôle reste largement manuelle et fragmentée entre des centaines de petits intégrateurs, chaque projet industriel nécessitant une version spécifique — verrou que Vetaion cherche à lever par la robotique.
𝗔𝘃𝗲𝗰 : Visionaries Tomorrow et UVC Partners (co-chefs de file).
𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝗱𝗲 𝘃𝘂𝗲 : Si Vetaion réussit à automatiser ce processus, elle ne vend pas seulement des robots : elle redéfinit le modèle économique d'un segment entier de la sous-traitance industrielle qui emploie des dizaines de milliers de techniciens en Europe.
